report.summary: Chunk 10 of 14: __init__ validation/assignment and run() entry point with fail-closed logic.

handoff.purpose: TaskAttempt.__init__ validation and assignment, plus run() entry point with early fail-closed checks.

symbols.name: TaskAttempt.__init__
symbols.note: Validates inputs, sets instance attributes including self._gate, self._manager, self.branch, self.effect_key.

symbols.name: TaskAttempt.run
symbols.note: Entry point for attempt execution; performs early checks (storage, cancellation, base revision, ledger) and returns AttemptResult on failure.

claims.text: TaskSpec command gates currently require gate_cwd='.'; subdirectory execution is not implemented
claims.why: Code raises ValueError if task.gate_argv and str(task.gate_cwd) != '.'.

claims.text: FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS beats the plain pytest_gate default but loses to an explicit gate/gate_argv override, matching the existing 'explicit beats implicit' precedence above.
claims.why: Code checks gate, then gate_argv, then correctness_before_state, else pytest_gate. The comment describes this precedence accurately.

claims.text: Lazy import: daedalus.eval.correctness imports daedalus.spine.attempt (READ_ONLY_REPO_VERBS) at ITS module top level, so importing it from THIS module's top level would be circular; by the time __init__ actually runs, both modules are already fully loaded.
claims.why: Circular import claim cannot be verified from this chunk alone; relies on module structure outside this file.

claims.text: correctness_gate is the existing, tested instrument (its own docstring: 'Signature and return type match the attempt's gate contract exactly') -- this wires it rather than re-deriving its fail-closed-on-an-unverified-receipt behaviour here.
claims.why: Refers to correctness_gate's docstring and behavior not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Default ON because the leak is unbounded: one ref per attempt, in the SHARED .git, forever. Off is for an operator who wants the branch left behind for forensics -- the patch bytes are already persisted separately, so this costs nothing but a ref.
claims.why: Comment describes the rationale for self._reap_enabled = bool(reap) defaulting to True (since reap default is True).

claims.text: Derived from the task, plus a nonce so a retry of the SAME task does not collide with the branch its predecessor left behind (and so resolve_by_effect can tell two attempts apart in the world).
claims.why: self.branch includes uuid hex, ensuring uniqueness even for same task_id and digest.

claims.text: Filled in by run() from the fresh worktree, BEFORE the runner is invoked. None until then, and None afterwards for a worktree whose .git was not the expected pointer file.
claims.why: Refers to self._admin_dir being set in run() which is not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: Attempt the task and return an AttemptResult. Never raises.
claims.why: run() always returns AttemptResult via finish() and catches exceptions returning error states.

claims.text: The returned artifact is data. Applying it to the primary checkout is a separate, human-invoked act that this module intentionally does not provide.
claims.why: Refers to artifact not defined in this chunk; not verifiable.

claims.text: Resolving the base is a READ of the primary checkout, not an effect, so it happens before the intent -- the payload can then name the exact revision the candidate was built on.
claims.why: Refers to _resolve_base() which is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: No durable record is possible, so no effect may be performed.
claims.why: If ledger is unavailable, run() returns STATE_WORKTREE_FAILED and does not proceed to runner.

observations.what: Imports correctness_gate inside __init__ to avoid circular import; this is a valid pattern but makes the gate assignment depend on runtime availability.
run() uses a nested function finish() to build AttemptResult; early returns are used for all error paths, ensuring no unhandled exception escapes.
The method _resolve_base() and _get_ledger() are called but not defined in this chunk; their behavior is unknown.
